title: Eleanor Roosevelt: Best First Lady
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Eleanor Roosevelt, covering her childhood after her parents' deaths, her marriage to Franklin Delano Roosevelt and the Lucy Mercer affair, her volunteering and activism, her unusually active role as First Lady (press conferences, newspaper column, radio, road trips), her work with Arthur Dale and the Scott's Run coal miners, her civil rights advocacy including the 1939 Marian Anderson concert at the Lincoln Memorial, her opposition to Japanese American internment, her relationship with Lorena Hickok, her Val-Kill circle, her role at the United Nations including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and her death in 1962. The episode closes with a listener mail segment about a TV station with a pool.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce Eleanor Roosevelt as the longest-serving First Lady and note how widely she was admired.

segments.title: Roosevelt family and early life
segments.summary: Eleanor's birth in 1884 into the Roosevelt family, the deaths of her mother and father, her upbringing with her grandmother, her schooling in England, and her early debutante years.

segments.title: Marriage to Franklin and Sarah Roosevelt
segments.summary: Eleanor and Franklin's courtship as fifth cousins, their 1905 marriage, and the controlling influence of Sarah Delano Roosevelt over the family.

segments.title: Lucy Mercer affair and polio
segments.summary: Eleanor discovers Franklin's affair with her secretary Lucy Mercer, the couple stays together, and Franklin is later stricken with polio.

segments.title: Eleanor's character and motherhood
segments.summary: Discussion of Eleanor's self-consciousness, her role as her husband's partner, and her strained relationship with her six children and Sarah.

segments.title: Political wife years and growing influence
segments.summary: Eleanor's entry into political life as Franklin's career rose, including his time as Assistant Secretary of the Navy and her growing role helping write speeches and strategize.

segments.title: Changing views and moral growth
segments.summary: Josh describes how Eleanor moved from the prejudices of her social class, including antisemitism and attitudes toward Black servants, to advocacy for Jewish refugees, civil rights, and women's rights.

segments.title: Volunteering, activism and early organizations
segments.summary: Eleanor's wartime volunteering with the Red Cross, work as a translator at the Paris Peace Conference, and involvement with the League of Women Voters.

segments.title: Democratic Party platform, Val-Kill Industries and labor work
segments.summary: Eleanor was shut out of a DNC committee on women's suffrage, co-founded the Val-Kill Industries furniture collective, and joined the Women's Trade Union League; hosts discuss child labor.

segments.title: First Lady firsts and Civilian Defense
segments.summary: Eleanor's unprecedented activities as First Lady, including press conferences, a newspaper column and radio show, and her role as assistant director of Civilian Defense, which drew criticism and led her to step down after a year.

segments.title: Road trips and travels across America
segments.summary: Eleanor's extensive travel, including her blue roadster and over 300,000 miles visiting nearly every state, reporting back to FDR.

segments.title: Relationship with Lorena Hickok
segments.summary: Eleanor's close relationship with AP reporter Lorena Hickok, which historians now generally believe was romantic, and the 1933 New England and Quebec trip.

segments.title: Hickok letter reading and marriage context
segments.summary: Chuck reads a letter excerpt from Hickok to Eleanor and the hosts discuss what it suggests, along with Franklin's affair and the couple's marriage.

segments.title: Arthur Dale and Scott's Run
segments.summary: Eleanor's visit to Scott's Run, West Virginia, which inspired the planned community Arthur Dale, and her long involvement with the town and its high school graduations.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode ad break.

segments.title: Civil rights advocacy
segments.summary: Eleanor's anti-racism and civil rights work, including NAACP lobbying, resignation from the DAR over Marian Anderson, the 1939 Lincoln Memorial concert, and the Birmingham seating incident with Mary McLeod Bethune.

segments.title: Japanese American internment
segments.summary: Eleanor visited a Japanese American internment camp and urged that the camps be closed, despite the executive order issued by FDR.

segments.title: Writing, radio and television work
segments.summary: Eleanor's prolific writing, including the My Day column and magazine advice column, memoirs, radio and NBC shows, and the Prospects of Mankind program.

segments.title: Podcast rankings tangent
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck briefly discuss podcast rankings and their international popularity.

segments.title: Val-Kill friendships and Earl Miller
segments.summary: Eleanor's close friendships with gay women including Esther Everett Lape, Elizabeth Read, Marion Dickerman and Nancy Cook, and the role of bodyguard Earl Miller, whom historians suspect had an affair with her and who encouraged her public confidence. Her pistol and the Klan bounty are mentioned.

segments.title: United Nations and Universal Declaration of Human Rights
segments.summary: After FDR's death in 1945, Truman appointed Eleanor to the US delegation to the UN, where she served on Committee Three, opposed forced repatriation of refugees, and helped author the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

segments.title: Death and legacy
segments.summary: Eleanor's death in 1962 at age 78 at her Upper East Side home, and her role in getting Frances Perkins into FDR's cabinet.

segments.title: Frances Perkins and future episode banter
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Frances Perkins as the first woman cabinet member and mention possible future episodes on Mary Tyler Moore and Chuck's pick.

segments.title: Listener mail: TV station with a pool
segments.summary: Alex writes about a TV station in a former motel building that has a pool, following up on a Selects episode about the fairness doctrine.

segments.title: Listener mail call-to-action
segments.summary: Josh invites listeners to send in their own stories by email.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck gives the show credits and directs listeners to find more podcasts on iHeartRadio.
